boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named, under-21-safe places and programs in Philadelphia with direct evidence of free admission or free public access.

cards.title: See the work at Temple Contemporary
cards.subtitle: Tyler School of Art and Architecture, 2001 N. 13th St.
cards.notes: Enter Tyler through the Norris Street entrance and spend time with the current gallery installation; confirm public hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Temple gallery explicitly free and open to all.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Contemporary describes its gallery as a university-based public space that is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; enter via Tyler's Norris Street entrance.

cards.title: Sketch among the Wagner specimens
cards.subtitle: 1700 W. Montgomery Ave., near Main Campus
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided look through the Victorian natural-history exhibit hall, or bring a pencil and paper for a specimen-sketching pause.
cards.short_summary: A nearby natural-history museum with free visits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wagner Free Institute states that its landmark museum is free to visit.
cards.access_notes: Museum hours listed by the Wagner are Tuesday–Friday, 9:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., plus select first Saturdays; register to visit as directed.

cards.entity_name: Beyond the Page: Exploring the Cultural, Historical, and Scholarly Record
cards.title: Join a Beyond the Page program
cards.subtitle: Temple University Libraries, Main Campus
cards.notes: Check the library calendar for a lecture, book talk, exhibition, or panel, then invite a friend to attend and discuss it afterward.
cards.short_summary: Temple Libraries’ public-program series is free and open to all.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple states that Beyond the Page lectures, book talks, exhibitions, and panels are free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Programs occur during fall and spring semesters; check the library calendar for the current schedule and venue.

cards.title: Read the exhibits around the Liberty Bell
cards.subtitle: 526 Market St., Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Go first-come, first-served, pass through security, and take time with the interpretive exhibits as well as the bell itself.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that Liberty Bell Center admission is free and no tickets are required.
cards.source_title: Visiting the Liberty Bell Center | National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m. according to NPS; entry is first-come, first-served and requires security screening.

cards.title: Walk through the President’s House Site
cards.subtitle: Independence National Historical Park, Philadelphia
cards.notes: Use the outdoor site’s interpretive material as a shared history walk, then compare the questions or details each person noticed.
cards.short_summary: An Independence park exhibit with no fee or ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the President's House Site as requiring no ticket and having no fee.
cards.source_title: Field Trips FAQs | Independence National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the site among student-friendly locations with no ticket and no fee; follow park guidance during your visit.

cards.title: Watch the Franklin Court printing demonstration
cards.subtitle: Independence National Historical Park, Philadelphia
cards.notes: Pair up to observe the eighteenth-century-style printing demonstration and trade one fact each person learned before leaving the site.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on historic printing stop without a fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says the Franklin Court Printing Office requires no ticket and has no fee.
cards.source_title: Field Trips FAQs | Independence National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: NPS describes this as a student-friendly site; verify same-day operating information with the park before travel.

cards.title: Examine originals at Great Essentials
cards.subtitle: West Wing, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Make a short document-focused stop and compare how each person reads the original printed material from the 1700s on display.
cards.short_summary: A free Independence park exhibit featuring original documents.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says the Great Essentials exhibit requires no ticket and has no fee.
cards.source_title: Field Trips FAQs | Independence National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the West Wing exhibit among locations with no ticket requirement and no fee; check park updates before visiting.

cards.title: Use the exhibits at Independence Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: 6th and Market Streets, Philadelphia
cards.notes: Meet at the big map, explore the interactive exhibits, and use the ranger desk to orient a no-cost historic-district walking plan.
cards.short_summary: A free-entry orientation stop with park exhibits and Wi-Fi.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states there is no fee to enter the Independence Visitor Center.
cards.source_title: Welcome to the Independence Visitor Center | National Park Service
cards.access_notes: NPS lists daily hours and notes free Wi-Fi; check the page for current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Take the Rocky Steps together
cards.subtitle: 2600 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia
cards.notes: Use the public steps for a quick walk, then take a group photo near the bronze Rocky statue without entering the museum.
cards.short_summary: A free public-art and staircase stop on the Parkway.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia Visitor Center states that visiting the Rocky Statue is completely free.
cards.source_title: The Rocky Statue and Rocky Steps | Philadelphia Visitor Center
cards.access_notes: The visitor center lists the site as open and accessible to the public; museum entry is separate and is not needed for this activity.

cards.title: Meet at the LOVE Sculpture
cards.subtitle: LOVE Park, 15th Street and JFK Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the sculpture and surrounding public park as a photo-and-walk meeting point, leaving time to look at the fountain and seating areas.
cards.short_summary: A free photo stop at Philadelphia’s landmark LOVE sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia Visitor Center states that photos at the iconic LOVE Sculpture are free.
cards.source_title: Where to Find Philly Visitor Centers in Summer 2026 | Visit Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: LOVE Park is open and accessible to the public; the cited source notes that a line can form for photos.
